grade_age: Grade 4 (age 9-10) - a DIFFERENT administration/year than the already-merged NY Grade 4 Science June 2022 batch (research/pipeline/ny-g4-science-2022/). Chosen specifically to target science's current gap: Age 9 High Achiever completely empty (0 items), Age 10 High Achiever thin (6 items).

deferred_reasons.5: Diagram shows a mature tomato-type parent plant with fruit, and four candidate young-plant images (A-D, one grass-like, one corn-like, one flowering plant, one tomato-seedling-like) that the student must visually compare to identify which is the offspring - genuinely visual pattern-matching with no reliable way to restate the four candidate images' distinguishing features in text without risking fabricating visual detail not actually verifiable from a PDF read.
deferred_reasons.9: Four labeled diagrams of the same tree branch across four seasons (varying amounts of leaves) that the student must visually compare to identify which one is winter/January - genuinely visual, same class of defect as the electrical-diagram-comparison item excluded from the 2022 NY Grade 4 batch.
deferred_reasons.31-45: Part II of this test is entirely open-ended/constructed-response (describe evidence, fill in a data table, estimate a value, explain in writing) with no fixed multiple-choice answer - excluded per this pipeline's standing rule against no-fixed-answer items, consistent with every prior batch including the 2022 NY Grade 4 batch.

note: Unlike the 2022 NY Grade 4 batch (which had no separate answer key and relied on the two worked sample questions plus unambiguous grade-4 phrasing), this 2019 batch's official Excel scoring key (els62019-sk.xlsx) was downloaded and parsed directly for all 30 Part I answers, giving explicit answer-key confidence for every extracted item rather than inferred confidence. All 28 usable items' answers were cross-checked against the key programmatically (extracted via zipfile/XML parsing of the .xlsx) and every one also matches straightforward grade-4 science reasoning from the question text itself (e.g. Q16 'how long for Earth to complete one path around the Sun' = D 'one year'), so there is no answer-key/reasoning conflict to flag. Items 5 and 9 (image-dependent, deferred) were excluded from this cross-check since they aren't going into the batch. Several items reference diagrams whose content is fully restated in the question text or not actually needed to answer (item 1: pond diagram with all objects named in text; item 8: butterfly life-cycle diagram, generic labeled cycle; item 17: moon-phase diagram, all phases named in text; item 22: magnet/car/wood diagram, fully describable as 'car must contain metal for magnet to move it'; item 26: four stacked boxes with masses labeled, stacking order stated; item 29: clothesline/pulley diagram, wheel-and-rope mechanism describable in text) - these were judged usable on the same basis as the 2022 batch's equivalent items.
